page.layout: One page of text, a single column. Running head at top with page number at top right. Poem title and subtitle centred, then one poem of sixteen lines, then a second heading and a short epigram in italic below.

p.i: Portus, & afflictis statio tutissima rebus, Et noftra miferis fola fub axe falus. Vindice quo floret pietas rediuiua parentum, Sanctaque cum ninea fimplicitate fides, Illius haud duro munufcula fufcipe vultu, Mente tuus tota qui cupit effe cliens. Qui vagus, exul, inops, terra iactatur & vnda, Per mala qua fallax omnia mundus habet. Dum ferus hinc fauit veterani exercitus hoftis, Dum tonat horrificas Principis aula minas, Dum niuibus canent imperuia culmina montes, Dum valles nimiis impediuntur aquis. Post mala tot feffus velut Athida ftratus ad aram Ante tuos fupplex offero dona pedes. Ingenij fterilis tenui de meffe maniplos Quos dat non fallax fed male cultus ager. Si placeant librum, fi non, ampletere mentem, Maius erit voto fi fit vtrunque meo.
Carmina Mellinum patrio sale tingere iussit Dum parcit famæ, Musa, Catulle, tuæ.

page.notes: The initial letters P (of Portus) and C (of Carmina) are large woodcut-style drop capitals and are joined to their words. The poem appears set in italic throughout. Long s is transcribed as plain s. Ligatures in "iactatur" and "ftatus" are read as ct and st. The word "famæ" in the epigram has a doubtful final letter, read as æ. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword and no signature are visible on this page.
